title: Breathless and unsteady
summary: Woman in her early sixties, living alone, with severe COPD and bilateral knee osteoarthritis. The PIP2 says she walks 'about 50 metres', but a physiotherapy walk test stopped at 18 metres and the adviser's notes show a short shop trip only managed with repeated stops. Aids for washing, toileting and dressing are recorded in the OT report but under-reported or absent on the form.
exercises: reliability: repeatedly and within a reasonable time (moving around)
aid recorded only in OT report
do not attribute getting to the toilet to activity 5

must_find.quote: If I'm doing potatoes I sit down to peel them.
Sits on her kitchen stool to prepare veg. Can't stand at cooker for more than a few mins.
Perching stool for kitchen offered. Patient declined, prefers to use her own kitchen stool.

gaps: No detail of whether she can safely cook a simple meal on the hob or only by microwave
How often she avoids cooking altogether on bad days
Whether lifting or draining a pan is ever done, and what happens when she tries
activities.draft_note: Needs to sit on a stool (an aid) to prepare food; 1c (microwave only) is the alternative at the same 2 points.
Form says no problems; nothing in other documents.

must_find.quote: Salbutamol 100 micrograms inhaler, 2 puffs as required, via spacer
Manages own inhalers, pharmacy blister pack for BP tablet. No issues.

gaps: Whether the spacer or blister pack is needed because of her condition rather than for convenience
No evidence of any difficulty using inhalers or rescue pack during exacerbations
activities.draft_note: Spacer and blister pack are mentioned, but nothing shows she needs them to manage medication; expert to decide whether 3b is arguable.

must_find.quote: I sit on it to wash. I couldn't stand in the shower long enough otherwise.
Shower seat: already in situ, provided 2024. Patient uses it for every shower.
Uses shower seat every time she showers. Showers twice a week, strip wash sitting at sink other days.

gaps: Whether she can wash her hair or lower body without help on bad chest days
Time taken to wash, including rests
activities.draft_note: Uses the shower seat every time she showers and sits to wash on other days; form, OT and notes agree.

must_find.quote: Rises from WC with difficulty due to knee pain.
Toilet frame fitted around WC on this visit. Patient tried it and found rising much easier.
No problems with the toilet itself.

gaps: Whether she has used the toilet frame regularly since it was fitted on 2026-06-02
Getting along the hall to the bathroom is not part of this activity; that evidence belongs to moving around
activities.draft_note: OT observed difficulty rising and fitted a toilet frame; form and client do not mention it, so ongoing use needs confirming.

must_find.quote: Long-handled shoe horn issued. Patient demonstrated safe use and reports using it daily to put on her shoes.
Dressing: unable to flex knees enough to reach feet comfortably.
I can dress myself. It takes me a while and I sit on the bed to do it.

gaps: How she manages socks, which she says are the hardest part; no sock aid recorded
Whether 20 minutes with rests is within a reasonable time period
Adviser did not ask about dressing equipment
activities.draft_note: Long-handled shoe horn used daily, recorded only in the OT report.
No problems reported with speaking or hearing.
Reading glasses only, which descriptor a allows.
Sociable; goes to bingo monthly. No difficulty described.
Manages own bills and shopping; daughter only helped set up online banking.
Knows her area and finds her way; worry about getting breathless is physical, not psychological distress from a mental condition.

must_find.quote: I can walk about 50 metres before I need to stop and get my breath.
Walk abandoned at 18 metres when patient stopped due to breathlessness and right knee pain.
She then walked a further 12 metres before stopping again and declined to continue.
Patient reported today as an average day.
stops at next door's wall to lean and get breath, then again at the bus shelter, sometimes a third time.
Better days maybe 1 or 2 a week, when she can get to the shop with fewer stops.
On arrival she needed to sit on the shower seat for 2 to 3 minutes to recover her breath before she could continue.
If she needs to go again soon after she has to wait until she has her breath back.

gaps: Form estimate (about 50 m) conflicts with measured 18 m; the conflict should be explained, not ignored
Corner shop distance is paced by the adviser (approx. 80 m), not measured, and is only achieved with 2 to 3 stops over about 15 minutes
No record of how far she can walk on a better day before the first stop
Form says shop trip 'most days'; notes say about 3 days a week; a diary has been requested
activities.draft_note: Measured 18 m on an average day, with long recovery and a shorter second walk, so she cannot reliably go more than 20 m; better days are 1 to 2 a week.

must_not_claim: That she uses a rollator or walking frame (physio records she uses a stick and a rollator was not provided)
That she has had falls (physio records no falls in 12 months, one near-fall)
That she can walk 80 metres without stopping
That anxiety or a mental health condition affects her journeys
That she uses a sock aid or needs another person's help to dress
